newsitem.title: USA: Mobil, Shell set California alliance.
newsitem.headline: Mobil, Shell set California alliance.

text.p: Mobil Corp said Wednesday it has agreed with Royal Dutch/Shell Group's Shell Oil Co to form a new company consisting of the California upstream operations of both companies.

The new company would represent the largest oil producer in California with combined proven reserves of more than one billion barrels of oil equivalent and production of approximately 250,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, Mobil said.
This is the result of talks between Mobil's domestic exploration and production business unit, Mobil Exploration & Producing U.S. Inc, and CalResources LLC, an upstream affiliate of Shell Oil.

After substantial study and discussions, Mobil and CalResources have signed a non-binding letter of understanding to establish a stand-alone California limited liability company focusing on both onshore and offshore exploration and production activities, Mobil said.

It would own a 40 percent equity interest in the proposed new company, with CalResources holding the remaining 60 percent interest. Mobil and CalResources currently produce about 100,000 barrels daily and 150,000 barrels daily, respectively, in California on an oil equivalent basis.
The tentative agreement establishes guidelines for the further evaluation of the proposed company, Mobil said.
Final agreement on the formation of the new alliance will be contingent upon reaching definitive agreements, regulatory approvals, and approval by directors of both parent companies.

"The proximity of Mobil and CalResources operations in two of California's largest heavy oil fields provides the opportunity to reduce expenses and capital costs, eliminate duplication and achieve economies of scale that the two companies could not achieve continuing to operate on a stand-alone basis," explained Mike Yeager, president and general manager of Mobil Exploration US.
The new company, which is expected to start operations by mid-1997, would be headquartered in Bakersfield, where Mobil and CalResources currently employ 500 and 875 people, respectively.

Mobil said its California-based refining, retail petroleum products marketing and pipeline operations are not part of the proposed new business and are not expected to be impacted by its establishment. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610
